title: IsSolvable instances for S2, S3, S4 in Mathlib

problemStatement.plain: Prove that the symmetric groups S2, S3, S4 are solvable groups via Lean 4/Mathlib IsSolvable instances. These are needed for the Abel-Ruffini theorem: polynomials of degree ≤ 4 are solvable by radicals.
whyMatters: Completing the Abel-Ruffini formalization: solvability of S2, S3, S4 ↔ solvability by radicals for degree ≤ 4
Provides type-class instances usable in other theorems via inferInstance
Demonstrates Lean 4 can handle the full solvability classification theorem

proven: perm_fin_2_solvable: IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 2)) — by inferInstance (Equiv.Perm (Fin 2) is commutative)
perm_fin_3_solvable: IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) — via short exact sequence A3 ◁ S3 with A3 ≅ Z/3
perm_fin_4_solvable: IsSolvable (Equiv.Perm (Fin 4)) — via solvability of A4 + short exact sequence
knownResults.goal: ACHIEVED: All IsSolvable instances for S2, S3, S4 proved in AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean with 0 sorries

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: IsSolvable instances for S2, S3, S4 and A2, A3, A4 are all proved in AbelRuffiniGaloisExtensions.lean (0 sorries). Key proofs: (1) S2: inferInstance (commutative group); (2) S3: short exact sequence A3 ◁ S3, A3 = alternatingGroup (Fin 3) proved commutative; (3) S4: via alternating_fin_4_solvable which uses Klein 4-group V4 as the key normal subgroup of A4.
insights: S2 ≅ Z/2 is abelian → IsSolvable by inferInstance (CommGroup implies IsSolvable)
S3 solvability: A3 = alternatingGroup(Fin 3) is commutative (3-element cyclic), S3/A3 ≅ Z/2 → solvable via isSolvable_of_comm + IsSolvable.isAbove
A4 solvability: klein_four = V4 = {e, (12)(34), (13)(24), (14)(23)} is normal in A4, A4/V4 ≅ Z/3, V4 abelian
S4 solvability follows: A4 normal in S4, S4/A4 ≅ Z/2, apply IsSolvable.isAbove to A4 solvability
Key Mathlib lemmas: IsSolvable.isAbove (quotient by normal solvable group → solvable), IsSolvable_of_isSolvable_quot (converse)

approaches.name: Type-class instances via series
approaches.description: Prove IsSolvable as instances using the composition series S_n ⊃ A_n ⊃ ... ⊃ {e}
